title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · Par9】We were interested in whether baseline expression of the target gene in a MASLD-relevant cell lineage was associated with changes in liver function during treatment with the corresponding drug class. Therefore, we focused on monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression as a transcriptomic feature that may characterize interindividual heterogeneity in liver-related biochemical changes during SGLT2 inhibitor treatment. Specifically, this study investigated whether baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with changes in the FIB-4 index after 6 months of luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD.

【Background · abstract-1-1】Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. We investigated the association between monocyte mRNA expression of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), the molecular target of luseogliflozin, and changes in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index during treatment with this agent.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and participants · Par10】This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from participants with type 2 diabetes and hepatic steatosis corresponding to MASLD, who attended the outpatient Department of Internal Medicine at Nerima Hikarigaoka Hospital between October 2023 and March 2026. MASLD was defined as imaging-confirmed hepatic steatosis together with at least one cardiometabolic risk factor; all included participants met this criterion because they had type 2 diabetes [14]. All regularly followed people with type 2 diabetes and fatty liver disease were screened for eligibility. Because the screened population was restricted to participants with type 2 diabetes, people with type 1 diabetes were not included in the initial study population. Eligible participants had type 2 diabetes and imaging-confirmed hepatic steatosis before luseogliflozin initiation [14]; no prior use of other SGLT2 inhibitors; and at least 6 months of luseogliflozin treatment as of March 2026. Luseogliflozin was initiated and continued at 2.5 mg/day. Participants were excluded for age <20 years as of March 2026; pregnancy; active cancer; renal replacement therapy or estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <15 mL/min/1.73 m2; absence of baseline monocyte samples; low purity of isolated monocytes, defined as CD14-positive cells <80%; missing data; insufficient residual serum; changes in antidiabetic or lipid-lowering medications within 6 months, except insulin dose adjustment; baseline hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) >10%; temporary interruption of luseogliflozin because of adverse events; or dose escalation to 5 mg/day within 6 months. Peripheral blood samples for monocyte isolation had been prospectively collected at SGLT2 inhibitor initiation from consenting participants with type 2 diabetes under an Institutional Review Board-approved prospective observational protocol. Samples for polymerase chain reaction analysis were processed on the collection day and stored at −80 °C according to the institutional protocol. Participants with baseline HbA1c >10% were excluded because they may require prior insulin therapy for severe hyperglycemia or be at risk of acute metabolic decompensation, making them unsuitable for evaluating luseogliflozin effects. During the study period, 143 people with type 2 diabetes and MASLD had received luseogliflozin treatment for at least 6 months. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 82 participants were included in the final analysis (Fig. 1). The primary outcome was the change in the FIB-4 index over 6 months. The prospective monocyte collection and analysis and the retrospective analysis of clinical and laboratory data related to luseogliflozin treatment were approved by the Institutional Review Board. All participants provided written informed consent for monocyte collection and analysis. Additional consent for retrospective clinical data analysis was waived by the Institutional Review Board, and study information was disclosed using an opt-out approach.

【Methods · abstract-2-1】This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was measured using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation. Changes were calculated as the 6-month value minus the baseline value; therefore, negative values indicated reductions.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · Par20】Finally, to determine whether baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was independently associated with change in the FIB-4 index, simple and multiple linear regression analyses were performed with change in the FIB-4 index at 6 months as the dependent variable. In simple linear regression analyses of baseline clinical parameters, waist circumference (β = −0.023, P = 0.003), AST (β = −0.450, P = 0.003), eGFR (β = 0.011, P = 0.022), platelet counts (β = 1.393, P < 0.001), hsCRP (β = −0.177, P = 0.028), baseline FIB-4 index (β = −0.760, P < 0.001), and monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression (β = −0.122, P < 0.001) were significantly associated with change in the FIB-4 index (Supplementary Table S4). In the multiple regression analysis, Model 1 included variables selected using a stepwise procedure (age and baseline FIB-4 index), and monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained significantly associated with change in the FIB-4 index (β = −0.066, P < 0.001; Table 4). In Model 2, additional adjustment was made for baseline waist circumference and HbA1c, together with the variables included in Model 1, and monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained significantly associated with change in the FIB-4 index (β = −0.064, P < 0.001; Table 4). Additionally, in Model 3, additional adjustment was made for the changes in waist circumference, HbA1c, and ALT, together with the variables included in Model 1, and monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained significantly associated with change in the FIB-4 index (β = −0.064, P < 0.001; Table 4). Furthermore, in two additional exploratory sensitivity analyses, baseline duration of diabetes, waist circumference, HbA1c, eGFR, and hsCRP were added to the variables included in Model 1. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained significantly associated both with the change in the FIB-4 index (β = −0.068, P < 0.001; Supplementary Table S5) and with the FIB-4 index at 6 months (β = −0.068, P < 0.001; Supplementary Table S6) after full adjustment. These findings support an association between baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and the magnitude of FIB-4 index reduction during luseogliflozin treatment.

【Results · abstract-3-1】After 6 months, waist circumference, hemoglobin A1c, liver enzyme levels, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and the FIB-4 index decreased significantly. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the change in the FIB-4 index, indicating that higher baseline expression was associated with a greater reduction. In multiple regression analyses, natural-log-transformed baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained associated with the change in the FIB-4 index after adjustment for baseline clinical variables.
